messages:
jamie: quick follow-up from today's all-hands re: budget/runway and procurement changes. posting answers here so folks can catch up.

olivia: what's the runway number if we hit downside sales? slides showed two lines.

elaine: baseline ~18 months. downside (slower sales + full hiring cadence) ~13-14 months. we built in hiring pause levers if needed.

matt: burn snapshot: ~$5.5M/month today; with planned revenue lift net burn falls toward ~$3.0-3.5M/mo by year end in baseline. model linked below.

jamie: @matt share the model and which roles are prioritized.

matt: link: https://short.link/redwood-budget-2026 (view). prioritized hires: 2 infra SREs, 1 security eng, 2 account executives. others are deferrable.

devon: procurement update: new approvals start Mon. >=$10k needs finance + cost-owner signoff; >=$50k needs exec sponsor. default card limit $5k.

olivia: vendor onboarding SLA concern  we have an urgent integration. new vendors can take up to 7 days?

devon: standard is 3 business days; new vendors up to 7. for urgent cases tag @devon + @finance-bot and mark "expedite"; aim for 48-72 hours but legal/security still required.

jamie: can you paste the PO fields so teams know what to fill?

devon: PO fields: vendor_name, amount, cost_center, justification, contract_term, contact, expedite_flag. approvals: cost-owner -> finance -> exec (if >=50k).

olivia: any change to Dedicated reserved capacity approvals? engineers need clarity for proposals.

matt: Dedicated still approved but new large commits require a 9-12 month ROI business case. i'll share a one-pager with assumptions (throughput uplift, ops savings, quantization gains).

jamie: request: can leadership post a short FAQ in #all-hands summarizing thresholds and runway key points for folks who missed the end?

elaine: yes  i'll post a pinned FAQ and a 2-min Loom explaining the new procurement flow.

finance-bot: Procurement workflow updated 2026-03-23T15:10:00Z. Use /po-request to begin. :robot_face:

jamie: thanks all, closing thread.
